affiliations.date_precision: three-month appointment; exact months not stated in the oral history
affiliations.research_notes: Andrade's own chronology places this three-month job directly before her government applications. She applied to an office then called OWI; by the time she received the job it was OSS. No intervening employment is described.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Tulane University in New Orleans / Newcomb
affiliations.research_notes: This is a documented earlier pre-OSS teaching appointment. It is not presented as Andrade's immediate predecessor because her oral history establishes later employment.

affiliations.role_title: chemical-engineering student and Army ROTC cadet
affiliations.date_precision: entered in fall 1938; graduated and was commissioned in 1943
affiliations.research_notes: The institutional biography documents a direct sequence from college and ROTC to commission, active duty, Infantry School, and immediate OSS assignment. Student status is not classified as employment.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Bordeaux branch of the family company
affiliations.date_precision: began at the start of the Second World War and ended with wartime internment
affiliations.research_notes: Two independent reputable profiles support the apprenticeship and intervening internment/escape chronology before Sichel enlisted in the U.S. Army. This claim attaches only to the M. F. index row and does not merge the adjacent Peter M. Sichel row.

claims.claim_text: Edna W. Andrade's best-supported immediate pre-OSS civilian employer was the Hecht Company in Washington, where she worked for three months as a floor manager.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I finally got this job as a so-called floor manager ... in the Hecht Company
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Andrade recalled a three-month Hecht Company floor-manager job, leaving it, applying for government work, and receiving a position that had become part of OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact Edna W. Andrade index name, her full Edna Davis Wright Andrade name in the Smithsonian transcript, and her described OSS Visual Presentation work align with the existing CIA identity evidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Her first-person narrative supplies a continuous Hecht-to-government-application-to-OSS sequence and describes no intervening employment.
claims.match_notes: The source supports strong chronological proximity rather than an explicit phrase such as 'recruited from'; the temporal basis is therefore strongly date-bounded, not explicit immediate.

claims.claim_text: The Hecht Company is the last civilian employer documented in Andrade's own chronology before her OSS appointment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: After describing the Hecht job and her departure after three months, Andrade immediately recounted applying for government positions and entering the office that became OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The full-name and wartime-role details in the Smithsonian oral history match the indexed Edna W. Andrade and the existing CIA institutional biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: The oral history provides a sequential narrative and no later civilian employer before OSS; exact calendar months remain unstated.
claims.match_notes: This claim identifies the last documented employer; it does not assert that no undocumented short-term activity occurred.

claims.claim_text: From 1939 through spring 1941, Andrade taught drawing and design at Newcomb College in New Orleans.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Andrade described a Tulane/Newcomb art-school appointment lasting two academic years and discussed the drawing-and-design curriculum she taught there.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The first-person transcript gives Andrade's full name and a career chronology consistent with the indexed OSS visual artist.
claims.temporal_assessment: She dated the appointment to 1939 through spring 1941, before her marriage, move, Hecht employment, and OSS work.
claims.match_notes: Newcomb is modeled as employment, not education, and is kept separate from the later Hecht job.

sources.locator_override: Transcript discussion of the Newcomb art-school appointment and two academic years

claims.claim_text: LaGueux was a chemical-engineering student and Army ROTC cadet at Rhode Island State College before his 1943 commission and direct Army-to-OSS path.
claims.evidence_excerpt: In 1943, he graduated with a Bachelor of Science Degree in Chemical Engineering and was commissioned
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The university biography places LaGueux at the institution from fall 1938 until his 1943 degree and commission, followed by active duty, Infantry School, and immediate OSS assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact Conrad F./E. LaGueux name, Captain rank, Pawtucket origin, URI chronology, Army commission and specific OSS operational history provide a high-confidence match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The institutional chronology directly connects graduation and commission to May 1943 active duty and subsequent OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: The college is recorded as a student affiliation, never as an employer. No reliable civilian employer has yet been identified.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Peter M. F. Sichel is strongly matched to Peter Max Ferdinand Sichel, while the adjacent Peter M. Sichel row remains a separate unresolved source record.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Independent profiles give the full Peter Max Ferdinand Sichel name and the same refugee, Army, OSS, and wine-trade chronology already documented for this entity.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The unusually specific M. F. initials match Peter Max Ferdinand Sichel; the NARA page also contains an adjacent Peter M. row with a different service number, so the source records are not merged.
claims.temporal_assessment: The profiles cover Sichel's prewar apprenticeship, wartime displacement, 1941 Army enlistment, and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Identity is high-confidence for the M. F. row, but Box 709 remains critical for service-number-level resolution of the adjacent row.

claims.claim_text: Peter M. F. Sichel's last documented civilian employment before U.S. Army service was an apprenticeship with the Bordeaux branch of H. Sichel Söhne.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Peter Max Sichel was just starting an apprenticeship with the Bordeaux branch
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An interview-based profile says Sichel began the Bordeaux-branch apprenticeship at the start of the war; a separate obituary corroborates the company, Bordeaux, internment, escape, and 1941 enlistment chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The full Peter Max Ferdinand Sichel name, matching M. F. initials, family company, refugee history, Army enlistment and OSS career support a high-confidence identity match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The apprenticeship preceded forced internment and escape, which in turn preceded Sichel's 1941 arrival in the United States and Army enlistment.
claims.match_notes: The known intervening status was wartime internment and displacement, not another identified employer. The claim is attached only to the M. F. entity.

research_attempts.query_text: "Edna W Andrade" OSS employer; "Edna Andrade" Hecht Company; Smithsonian oral history transcript; NARA index; CIA biography; institutional and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar art-school employment, later gallery biographies without wartime chronology, and discovery-only summaries were rejected for the immediate-employer claim.
research_attempts.research_notes: Andrade's Smithsonian oral history supports Hecht Company as the strongly date-bounded immediate and last civilian employer before OSS and Newcomb College as earlier documented employment.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 17 for exact appointment dates and official job titles.

research_attempts.query_text: "Mort S Bobrow" OSS; employer 1940; occupation; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; obituary; university, newspaper, directory and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Common-name results, postwar civic and professional references, bare search snippets, and sources lacking a pre-OSS date were rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: The completed online protocol supports University of Washington student status followed by Army Mandarin training and OSS China service. It did not identify a reliable civilian employer.

research_attempts.query_text: "Edmund Michael Burke" OSS employer; "Edmund M Burke" Insurance Company of North America; NARA index; CIA biography; Penn, obituary, directory and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: The Insurance Company of North America claim appears only in an unreferenced tribute page and could not be corroborated in accessible official, institutional, directory or contemporary sources; postwar entertainment work was rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: Burke's identity and Penn football affiliation remain well supported, but the employer lead is retained only in the research trail and is not published as fact.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 93 and historical employer personnel records.

research_attempts.research_notes: Smith and Columbia student affiliations are documented, but accessible sources do not establish her own employer between study and the March 1943 OSS appointment.

research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar American Cyanamid and CIA employment, secondary commemorative pages without pre-service information, and summaries that conflated military assignment with civilian work were rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: URI documents a student-to-commission-to-Army-training-to-OSS sequence. No civilian employer before Army service is documented.

research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Namesake results, postwar references, and sources that did not distinguish the career Army assignment from civilian employment were rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: Official sources confirm a continuous career-Army path through leadership of the U.S. Military Mission to China and into OSS. The central immediate-affiliation question is answered.
